title: Network Reconnaissance
description: You're sitting on a Kali box (192.168.90.6) inside the DMZ of a Tennessee Eastman chemical plant. Somewhere across the network, a PLC is controlling a chemical process, Remote I/O modules are reading sensors and driving actuators, and an HMI is letting operators see what's happening. Two subnets, a router in between, and you don't have a map. Build one. Remember this is OT, so be mindful of what your scans might do to the systems you're probing.
objectives: Discover live hosts on your local DMZ subnet (192.168.90.0/24)
Discover hosts on the ICS subnet (192.168.95.0/24) beyond the router
Identify the PLC, HMI, Engineering Workstation, Remote I/O modules, and 3D plant sim
Determine what services and protocols are listening on each host
Access the HMI web interface and the PLC management dashboard — understand what each shows you
Find the Modbus-speaking devices and note how many there are
learning_points: OT networks are commonly segmented into zones — a DMZ, a control network, and sometimes a safety network
Modbus TCP (port 502) is one of the most common ICS protocols — and has zero built-in authentication
A router between zones may be running IDS (like Suricata) — your scans may be logged or blocked
Many ICS devices expose web interfaces for configuration that are often left at default credentials
The Tennessee Eastman process is a realistic chemical benchmark — feed mixing, reaction, separation, and recycle
things_to_think_about: What would happen if an aggressive nmap scan crashed a Remote I/O module mid-process?
The router sits on both subnets at .200 — what role does it play beyond routing?
How many Modbus devices did you find? Why are there more than just a PLC?
What services did you find that would never exist on a typical corporate network?
flag_hint: The flag is the Modbus slave ID shared by all Remote I/O devices concatenated with the total number of Remote I/O modules: FLAG{slaveid_count}
blue_team_check: The router at 192.168.95.200 runs Suricata IDS. After your recon, check its alert log. Did your scans trigger any signatures? What did the defenders see crossing between subnets?
